articles.title: How Travis Kelce scored a 21,000-sq-ft gilded age mansion for $5.35M, while the seller paid just $1.95M in 2023
articles.summary: NFL News: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce purchased a historic 21,000-square-foot lakefront mansion in Bratenahl, Ohio, months before marrying Taylor .
articles.body: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce purchased a historic 21,000-square-foot lakefront mansion in Bratenahl, Ohio, months before marrying Taylor Swift. He closed the deal in March 2026, negotiating the price down from $5.99 million to $5.35 million. The previous owner, a local construction firm, had picked it up for just $1.95 million in 2023, spent roughly a year restoring it, and relisted at a much higher price. The gap between those two numbers tells a bigger story than any celebrity headline can.What makes Travis Kelce's Bratenahl mansion worth $5.35 million?The estate, known as Moyenage, dates back to 1895 and sits along Lake Shore Boulevard in Bratenahl, a small lakefront village just a few miles from Kelce's hometown of Cleveland Heights. It spans 21,140 square feet across eight bedrooms, eight full and three half bathrooms, seven fireplaces, five garage spaces, and a heated in-ground pool. That is not a house. That is a compound.Original features like carved walnut walls, leaded glass, and marble were preserved throughout the restoration, while modern amenities were added to bring the property up to current luxury standards. The former ballroom was converted into a game room and home theater, and the gatehouse was transformed into a self-contained two-bedroom guest cottage. A new bluestone patio and heated pool overlooking Lake Erie were also added during the renovation.The Agency Cleveland agents David Ayers and Nick Zawitz, who handled both sides of the sale, described it as "a truly rare Great Lakes estate" that blends preservation with modern updates. They also confirmed it set a new price record for the Bratenahl shoreline.How did the seller turn a $1.95M buy into a $5.35M sale?This is where the deal gets genuinely interesting. Figurati Construction Group, a Northeast Ohio renovation firm, purchased the property for $1.95 million in 2023 and set about restoring it from the ground up. Once the work was done, the renovated estate hit the market in mid-2023 at an initial asking price of $6.99 million.It sat. For almost two and a half years.The asking price was reduced to $5.99 million in May 2025 before Kelce ultimately bought it for $5.35 million in March 2026, which works out to an 11 percent discount from the reduced price and 24 percent below the original list. Even for a buyer with deep pockets who clearly wanted this property near his roots, the numbers show he did not simply write a blank check.Real estate records show the home was acquired through an Ohio LLC formed just days before closing, with tax correspondence directed to André Eanes, Kelce's longtime business manager. The structure of the purchase is about as deliberate as the negotiation.Why did Travis Kelce choose Cleveland over Kansas City or New York?The location was not accidental. Kelce grew up in Cleveland Heights, and the Bratenahl property sits close enough to feel like home territory rather than a random luxury purchase on a celebrity's real estate map. He has spoken about his connection to the city openly."Getting Tay back to Cleveland and showing her my roots is always something I love doing," Kelce said on his New Heights podcast. His attachment to the area predates the relationship entirely.The sale was confirmed by The Agency Cleveland and was described by the agents as a record transaction for Bratenahl's Lake Erie shoreline. The purchase adds a third known U.S. property to Kelce's holdings, alongside a home in Kansas City, Missouri, and a 17,000-square-foot estate in Leawood, Kansas, where he and Swift got engaged in August 2025.The Moyenage deal is less about celebrity spending and more about a calculated return. Kelce bought a piece of Ohio history, got a meaningful discount despite being highly motivated, and brought one of Cleveland's oldest lakefront estates back into public conversation. For a region that does not always make the luxury real estate headlines, that is worth noting.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

We've compiled where the public is betting at sportsbooks, along with some notable wagers, and asked several oddsmakers at various sportsbooks around the country to find out where the sharp action has come in for this weekend's games.

Thomas Gable, sportsbook director at Borgata in Atlantic City: "Bears currently laying -4.5, down from opener of -5.5. We opened total at 47.5, got up to 49.5, saw buyback there. The total is now sitting at 48. With the Bears scoring as many points as they did in Week 1, I had a feeling this was going to get bet up by the public. Should be a good chess match between Ben Johnson and Brian Flores."

Joey Feazel, head NFL trader at Caesars Sportsbook: "We saw a lot of love for the Bears, as Caleb Williams went from 15-1 to +850 on Sunday to win MVP. Lookahead line was -3, opened -5.5, back down to -4.5. Lookahead total was 45.5, opened 48.5, down to 48. We're not seeing action on one side yet, just on the over. We saw plenty of points scored on the field, attracted bettors' attention. Public has definitely targeted the over."

Gable: "No real movement on the spread. Texans -2.5, touched 3 briefly and quickly back to -2.5. Total has been the big mover, down from 47.5, now down to 45.5. Not as much appetite on Cincinnati at +2.5."

Feazel: "A lot of love on the Bengals carrying over from the offseason in the underdog role. Texans offensively didn't look terrible, but defense wasn't great against Josh Allen in Week 1. Even split on the total."

Gable: "This one hasn't moved. The total is at 45.5, up a point from the opener. Not a ton written on this game on the side, pretty balanced action on what we've taken."

Feazel: "Leading into Chiefs-Broncos, the public was all over Denver and there was some anti-Chiefs money. That hasn't deterred the Broncos' faithful — still more money on the Broncos right now for us. It'll be interesting to see if we get some Jacksonville money leading into kickoff. Right now, one-way traffic on Denver -2.5."

Indianapolis Colts at Kansas City Chiefs

Gable: "Chiefs -6.5 right now, which is what we opened at. It's been pretty much all Kansas City money. Total of 48 is what we opened, it's now at 46.5. Not sure if this game touches 7, but a lot of public KC money coming in so far."

Feazel: "Two-way action on this game, we're sitting on a strong Kansas City -6.5 right now. Daniel Jones and the Colts didn't look great against the Ravens. I'd anticipate a little more Chiefs action as we get closer to game day."

Gable: "This has dropped. We opened Cowboys -4.5, but that was before Sunday Night Football was played so we hadn't seen Dallas on the field yet. Surprisingly, there has been some decent Commanders money here. We're sitting Cowboys -4, total of 50.5. I thought people might come back in here on Dallas, but in the early going, more Washington money on the spread than Dallas."

Feazel: "Commanders looked a little more competitive against Eagles, but public was on Cowboys. Seeing mostly Cowboys money, would anticipate that remaining the same. Seeing a little more under money."

articles.title: What happened to Nico Collins? Latest injury update after Texans star WR ruled out vs Bengals
articles.summary: NFL News: The Houston Texans received tough news ahead of their Week 2 game against the Cincinnati Bengals after wide receiver Nico Collins was ruled out with a.
articles.body: The Houston Texans received tough news ahead of their Week 2 game against the Cincinnati Bengals after wide receiver Nico Collins was ruled out with a hamstring injury. Collins picked up the issue during Wednesday’s practice and could not return to the field during the rest of the week.The Nico Collins injury came at a difficult time for Houston. The star receiver had just opened the 2026 season against the Buffalo Bills, catching seven passes on 10 targets for 75 yards and a touchdown. Now, the Texans will have to face Cincinnati without one of their most important offensive players.What is Nico Collins’ injury and will he play in Week 2?Collins is dealing with a Grade 1 hamstring injury that he suffered during Wednesday’s practice, according to league sources. He missed Thursday and Friday’s practices before the Texans officially ruled him out on their final injury report.The injury has been described as mild, but Houston has taken a cautious approach with its star receiver. Collins’ availability for Week 3 against the Indianapolis Colts remains uncertain, so the Texans will likely monitor his recovery closely over the next several days.That caution also comes from Collins’ injury history. A similar hamstring problem in 2024 forced him to miss five games and spend time on injured reserve. The Texans will therefore want to avoid rushing him back and risking another setback.Collins had already made an impact in the opening game of the season. He led Houston in receiving against Buffalo, finishing with seven receptions on 10 targets for 75 yards and a touchdown. His absence now leaves a major gap in C.J. Stroud’s passing attack.The Texans also entered the season with fewer options at wide receiver. Jayden Higgins is dealing with a torn ACL, while Tank Dell remains on injured reserve. Houston therefore has fewer proven receivers available to replace Collins. How will Texans replace Nico Collins against the Bengals?Houston is expected to use a committee approach at wide receiver against Cincinnati rather than asking one player to completely replace Collins.Adam J. Wexler explained the expected adjustment on Sportstalk 790.“If he does not play, they will not go into that game with four active wide receivers,” Wexler said. “They will activate somebody or elevate somebody from the practice squad at the bare minimum.”Wexler also explained that the fifth wide receiver could look different from the player Houston used in Week 1.“I don't think they would need to sign somebody at this point, following along with the Collins injury. So they'll suit up five, but there'll be a difference between the fifth wide receiver this week and the fifth wide receiver last week.”Kayshon Boutte, Xavier Hutchinson and Jaylin Noel could see more opportunities with Collins unavailable. Tight end Dalton Schultz could also become a bigger part of the passing game as Stroud looks for other reliable targets.The Texans will now try to move forward without their top receiver against Cincinnati. Collins’ injury does not currently appear to be a long-term problem, but his history with hamstring issues gives Houston another reason to take things slowly. His progress next week should provide a clearer picture of whether he can return against the Colts.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body:
Former NFL star LeSean McCoy has no problem with Pat McAfee's recent smoking fiasco.

The 2026-27 NFL season has marked a new era for Pat McAfee, as he recently made his debut on Monday Night Countdown.

Aside from that, McAfee continues his iconic 'The Pat McAfee Show,' where fans see a much more unfiltered version of the former NFL star.

Keeping that in mind, McAfee once again made headlines, but not for his sports take. Instead, he was allegedly seen smoking a marijuana joint on ESPN.

LeSean McCoy gives his verdict on Pat McAfee's smoking incident

2x Super Bowl champion LeSean McCoy sees nothing wrong with the viral clip where McAfee is allegedly putting down a lit joint while being on live TV.

"I'm a fan of Pat. I've always been a fan of Pat. The stuff he's doing right now, nobody's done. He's great on TV, great personality. Imagine a kicker doing these types of things," McCoy said.

He added, "I root for Pat, like I said, ain't nobody more powerful than him other than the president."

Some thought ESPN might punish McAfee for his smoking incident, but McCoy was in the other corner as he heaped nothing but praise on the former NFL kicker.

In fact, McCoy went as far as saying that McAfee is currently the most powerful person in the US, not named Donald Trump.

articles.title: Week 2 Fantasy Injury Report and Last Minute Waiver Wire Replacements
articles.summary: Injuries are already becoming a problem for fantasy football managers in 2026. We saw stars like A.J. Brown, Sam Darnold, Myles Garrett, and Zay Flowers exit in Week 1. In Thursday night's Week 2 opener between the Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions, Bills receiver D.J. Moore left with a shoulder injury and did not return.
articles.body:
Injuries are already becoming a problem for fantasy football managers in 2026. We saw stars like A.J. Brown, Sam Darnold, Myles Garrett, and Zay Flowers exit in Week 1. In Thursday night's Week 2 opener between the Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions, Bills receiver D.J. Moore left with a shoulder injury and did not return.

Other injury situations are likely to impact lineup decisions for Sunday's slate, but managers may still be able to find help on the waiver wire.

Here, you'll find a look at the latest from the Week 2 injury report , rankings for the top remaining plays on the schedule, and some sleepers who could potentially serve as last-minute options.

All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Darnold won't play for the Seattle Seahawks this week, which means we'll see Drew Lock against the Arizona Cardinals. The Atlanta Falcons have ruled out Michael Penix Jr. for the second straight week, while Tua Tagovailoa is listed as doubtful.

The Cincinnati Bengals have listed Joe Burrow as questionable with a back injury, though he's widely expected to face the Houston Texans on Sunday. The Minnesota Vikings have ruled out Kyler Murray (concussion), which means it'll be Carson Wentz against the Chicago Bears.

New Orleans Saints signal-caller Tyler Shough is coming off a 410-yard, three-touchdown performance and remains the top QB to consider grabbing off the wire. He did face a bad Detroit Lions defense in Week 1, but he has a ton of upside and is still only rostered in 49 percent of fantasy leagues.

Malik Willis, C.J. Stroud, and Bryce Young are other quarterbacks worth considering off the wire this week.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

The list of key RB injuries is quite short, though the Vikings have placed Jordan Mason (thumb) on injured reserve. The Denver Broncos have listed RJ Harvey (hamstring) as questionable.

Good running backs are in short supply this year, and the trend extends to the waiver wire. San Francisco 49ers rookie Kaelon Black is about the only wire option with a reasonable amount of upside in Week 2.

Black had a prominent role spelling Christian McCaffrey on the ground in Week 1, and he'll face a suspect Miami Dolphins defense on Sunday. He's not likely to be heavily involved in the passing game and is listed as questionable (groin), but he is rostered in just 42 percent of fantasy leagues.

Braelon Allen, Kendre Miller, Jonah Coleman, and Jaleel McLaughlin are other backs to consider, though they're largely more valuable as stash options than Week 2 fill-ins. Miller is the exception, as he did get some goal-line work for the Saints last week.

Several notable receivers will be out this week, in addition to Brown. Rookies Ja'Kobi Lane and De'Zhaun Stribling are headed to injured reserve, while Nico Collins, Jauan Jennings, Omar Cooper Jr., and Marvin Mims Jr. have been ruled out.

The Baltimore Ravens have listed Flowers as doubtful. Pittsburgh Steelers receiver Michael Pittman Jr. and Tampa Bay Buccaneers receiver Jalen McMillan are both listed as questionable.

Saints receiver Chris Olave is also questionable with a hamstring injury, which only boosts the value of Devaughn Vele.

Vele was already a strong waiver target after tallying seven catches for 69 yards and a touchdown in Week 1. He's been heavily added but is still available in over half of fantasy leagues.

Deebo Samuel, Denzel Boston, Caleb Douglas, and Dontayvion Wicks are other receivers worth considering that could have some real flex value in Week 2.

The Washington Commanders have ruled out tight end Chigoziem Okonkwo with a hamstring injury.

Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers is considered doubtful as he continues to recover from a knee procedure. This gives some solid value to teammate Michael Mayer, who caught six passes for 32 yards last week.

Mayer is still only rostered in 16 percent of fantasy leagues.

The list of other tight ends to consider adding this week includes Mike Gesicki, Dalton Schultz, and Terrance Ferguson.

*Fantasy roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: 1 Player With the Most to Prove on Every NFL Team Entering Week 2
articles.summary: We're only one game into Week 2, which means it's still very early in the NFL regular season. However, some players are already facing high-pressure situations before the calendar even turns to October.
articles.body:
We're only one game into Week 2, which means it's still very early in the NFL regular season. However, some players are already facing high-pressure situations before the calendar even turns to October.

Now, starters and high draft picks are rarely on the hot seat the same way that coaches are this early in the season—and a few coaches are dealing with remarkably warm seats—but that doesn't mean many of them don't have something to prove.

In fact, as we enter the season's second Sunday, every NFL franchise has at least one player who must meet lofty expectations, rebound from poor performances, or answer critical preseason questions that have yet to be answered.

Arizona Cardinals: WR Marvin Harrison Jr.

The Arizona Cardinals might just be better than most expected this season. The Cardinals certainly looked threatening during last Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers, a team that has made the playoffs in back-to-back seasons.

Arizona's offense, which racked up 393 yards in Week 1, was particularly impressive. However, wide receiver Marvin Harrison was not. The fourth overall pick in the 2024 draft impressed as a rookie but regressed in 2025 and was held to just one 33-yard catch in Week 1.

In the coming weeks, Harrison must prove that he can perform up to his draft stats. If he can't, his future in Arizona will become rather murky.

The Cardinals have a star tight end in Trey McBride, they just signed wideout Michael Wilson to a three-year, $75 million extension, and they just used the third overall pick on running back Jeremiyah Love . Harrison will be extension-eligible in the offseason, but Arizona can't pay everyone, and he could eventually be the odd man out.

To be clear, we won't actually see Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. in Week 2. The 26-year-old is working his way back from a torn ACL and is out for another week, though he is trending in the right direction.

"We're working," Penix said, per Daniel Flick of the Atlanta Journal-Constitution . "I'm close."

However, there aren't many players with more to prove entering Week 2. The 2024 first-round pick didn't play particularly well last season before the knee injury, and he may be running out of opportunities. A loaded 2027 draft class looms large, and the Falcons have three other quarterbacks on the current roster.

Atlanta was set to start Tua Tagovailoa in Week 1 before he suffered an oblique injury. Cooper Rush got the start instead, and the Falcons also have undrafted rookie Jack Strand in the QB room. If Penix wants to cement himself as a franchise signal-caller, he must get healthy, claim the starting gig, and never relinquish it.

Replacing a legitimate star is a challenge that usually comes with pressure. Baltimore Ravens center Jovaughn Gwyn, who is replacing Pro Bowler Tyler Linderbaum, is learning that firsthand.

Linderbaum had become a fixture of the Ravens' interior offensive line. Gwyn joined Baltimore on a one-year, $1.2 million contract this offseason.

While Gwyn performed well in the run game in Week 1, he drew a critical holding call that negated a touchdown. He also struggled in pass protection and was ranked last among pass blockers by Pro Football Focus . The 2023 seventh-round pick has shown promise but is not yet close to proving he can replace Linderbaum long-term.

2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 2 🏈

Buffalo Bills wide receiver Keon Coleman has fallen short of expectations since he was taken 33rd overall in 2024—to the point that franchise owner Terry Pegula felt the need to blame Coleman's selection on then-recently fired head coach Sean McDermott back in January.

Coleman very much looked like a difference-maker on Thursday night, tallying six receptions for 63 yards against the Detroit Lions. However, he has just 1,024 yards in 28 regular-season games and desperately needs to prove that he can perform at a high level consistently.

The Bills may need Coleman to prove himself immediately. Prized trade acquisition D.J. Moore exited Thursday's game with a shoulder injury and did not return, though ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Moore "has a chance" to play in Week 3.

The Carolina Panthers added a pair of marquee defenders in free agency, signing edge-rusher Jaelan Phillips and linebacker Devin Lloyd. Phillips, who recorded a sack and three quarterback pressures, was pretty solid in Week 1. Lloyd was less impressive.

While the former Jacksonville Jaguars star did record a whopping 13 tackles, he had one missed tackle and struggled mightily in coverage. He allowed six catches on seven targets for 58 yards, and Pro Football Focus graded him 65th overall among linebackers.

Carolina needs Lloyd to be a legitimate game-changer if its defense is going to be better than it was against the Bears in Week 1. Lloyd needs to prove that he's worth the three-year, $42 million contract he signed in free agency a few months ago.

The Chicago Bears offense was spectacular in Week 1, racking up 59 points and eventually pulling away from the Panthers. However, Chicago's defense, which surrendered 37 points, left plenty to be desired.

One of the week's worst performers was cornerback Tyrique Stevenson. In coverage, he allowed four completions on five targets for 77 yards, two touchdowns, and a perfect 158.3 passer rating.

Stevenson was a mostly reliable starter last season, and he needs to prove he can return to that form as soon as possible. The Bears need him to perform better, obviously, but the 26-year-old Stevenson is also in a contract year and is playing for a 2027 free-agent contract.

New Cincinnati Bengals defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence was more impactful in Week 1 than the raw numbers would suggest. He didn't record a tackle or sack, but he did log a quarterback hit , pushed into the backfield on multiple occasions, and allowed other defenders to make plays by commanding attention.

Still, Lawrence needs to prove that he can be a true game-wrecker for the Bengals, and he needs to do it consistently this season. Cincinnati is betting heavily on a return trip to the playoffs in 2026, and it traded the 10th overall pick in the draft to add Lawrence.

Fair or not, Lawrence is being asked to change the fortunes of a franchise that has been quite bad defensively in recent years.

The 28-year-old is signed through 2028 and should have several good years ahead of him, but he doesn't quite offer the long-term value of a high-upside rookie. If Lawrence is merely good, while a rookie like Caleb Downs or Francis Mauigoa becomes an instant star, it'll be hard to look back on the trade as a big win for the Bengals.

Deshaun Watson has been an absolute flop since the Cleveland Browns acquired him in a 2022 trade. He was booed at home by fans during the preseason, and there's a very real chance that if he doesn't play well and deliver an upset win in Week 2, Watson will be out of the starting lineup by Week 3.

The 31-year-old may not be able to mentally handle another unwelcoming home crowd.

According to Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com, "The pressure is getting to him. The criticism is getting to him. He is just tired of taking the heat all over the place."

Cleveland will probably be finished with Watson when his contract expires at the end of the season. However, he's going to have to show some signs of promise if he's going to play elsewhere in 2027 and beyond, and he may have to do it this week.

The Dallas Cowboys won't have promising linebacker DeMarvion Overshown in Week 2 because the Texas product is injured. Again.

A 2023 third-round pick, Overshown missed his rookie year with a torn ACL but flashed a ton of potential as a 12-game starter during his inaugural season. He recorded 90 tackles and five sacks in 2024, but he also suffered a second season-ending knee injury in Week 14. He returned for six games last season but then missed the final two contests with a concussion.

Overshown started in Week 1 but suffered a hamstring injury and is set to miss "one to two weeks," according to head coach Brian Schottenheimer (h/t Tommy Yarrish of the team's official website).

Playing in a contract year, Overshown needs to prove that he can get on the field, stay there, and play at the level he did two years ago.

You could reasonably say that every Denver Broncos player has a lot to prove entering Week 2. The Broncos were the best team in the AFC during the 2025 regular season but looked to be entirely outclassed against the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday night.

While nobody played particularly well for Denver in Week 1, wide receiver Jaylen Waddle was arguably the biggest disappointment. The Broncos acquired Waddle in a pre-draft trade with the Miami Dolphins that cost a first-round pick and more.

Adding Waddle was supposed to boost quarterback Bo Nix, unlock Denver's passing attack, and aid new offensive play-caller Davis Webb. After catching just one pass for two yards in his Denver debut, Waddle has a long way to go to prove that trading for him was worth it.

The Lions defense has looked atrocious through its first two games of the season, and most players on the unit should be looking to prove that they can be better. However, starting cornerback Rock Ya-Sin may have to prove himself just to hang onto his job.

Ya-Sin has been a liability more often than not this season and has allowed an opposing passer rating of 115.4 in coverage. On Thursday, he was also flagged for a costly holding penalty that negated a would-be interception in the red zone.

Last season, Ya-Sin was much more dependable in a part-time role and allowed an opposing passer rating of just 74.7. However, Detroit has been scrambling to fill voids in the secondary due to injuries and the release of Terrion Arnold. If Ya-Sin can't prove that he can return to his 2025 form, the Lions will need to look elsewhere for cornerback help.

As a unit, the Green Bay Packers offensive line was a major issue against the Minnesota Vikings last week. Jordan Love was sacked four times, was pressured repeatedly, and was forced into two critical fourth-quarter turnovers.

While left tackle Jordan Morgan can't bear all of the blame for his unit's poor performance, he certainly didn't help. The 2024 first-round pick struggled in pass protection throughout the game and was graded 57th among tackles in pass blocking by Pro Football Focus .

Morgan was already under a fair amount of pressure when the season began, as he's being asked to replace former starter Rasheed Walker. Entering Week 2, he'll be under immense pressure to prove that he's up to the challenge of starting on the left side.

Cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. may feel like an odd choice, as the two-time All-Pro has long been one of the Houston Texans' top defenders. However, the 25-year-old is also expected to be one of the very best defensive backs in the game.

Last offseason, Stingley signed a three-year, $90 million extension that made him the league's highest-paid defensive back at the time.

However, Stingley didn't perform like a top-tier corner during Houston's Week 1 loss to Buffalo. He recorded four tackles and a forced fumble, but he also allowed four completions for 68 yards and an opposing passer rating of 90.2 .

If the Texans hope to be title contenders this season, they need their defense to perform like the top-ranked unit it was a year ago. For that to happen, they need Stingley to do a better job of locking things down on the back end.

The Indianapolis Colts defense looked totally outmatched against the Ravens in Week 1. Baltimore racked up 506 total yards and 41 points en route to one of the most lopsided victories of the opening slate.

Plenty of players deserve blame for Indy's defensive meltdown. However, cornerback Justin Walley was particularly disappointing. The 2025 third-round pick made his first career start and surrendered six catches for 109 yards and a 118.7 opposing passer rating.

Walley missed his entire rookie season after suffering a torn ACL in training camp. The Minnesota product will undoubtedly earn more opportunities because of his draft status, but if he doesn't rebound quickly, his time as a 2026 starter could be rather brief.

During the 2025 draft, the Jacksonville Jaguars made an aggressive trade up to land cornerback and wide receiver Travis Hunter. The Jags gave up the fifth and 36th picks in 2025, their 2027 first-rounder, and more to snag Hunter at No. 2.

The collegiate two-way superstar was expected to fill a similar role in Jacksonville. However, he was mostly just OK as a rookie before suffering a season-ending LCL injury. He finished his inaugural campaign with 298 receiving yards and 15 tackles in seven games.

Hunter wasn't particularly impactful in Week 1, either. He logged four offensive snaps and 29 defensive snaps, and he finished with an eight-yard catch and a tackle.

Yes, Hunter is contributing on both sides of the ball. However, he hasn't come close to proving that he can be a quality two-way NFL player or that he's worth Jacksonville's hefty investment.

Last offseason, the Kansas City Chiefs used a first-round pick on Josh Simmons, hoping that he would fill the longstanding need for a starting left tackle.

Unfortunately, Simmons missed nine games during his rookie season due to a personal absence and a wrist injury. He wasn't particularly great when he was on the field, either, which left him with plenty to prove heading into Year 2.

Simmons wasn't a part of Kansas City's dominant Week 1 victory, as he was ruled out with a back injury. Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson got the start in Simmons' stead, and while Benson wasn't great (ranked 54th among tackles by PFF ), he wasn't any more of a liability than Simmons has been when healthy.

If Simmons hopes to lock down a starting job with the Chiefs, he has to get back on the field and prove that he is more than a replacement-level player.

Quarterback Kirk Cousins was mostly good in his Las Vegas Raiders debut. However, while he threw three touchdown passes and helped deliver the win, he also struggled to push the ball deep (5.3 yards per attempt) and tossed a pair of picks.

While Cousins' performance was enough against a Miami Dolphins team that might be the worst in the league, Cousins has to be better moving forward for a couple of reasons. For starters, the Raiders aren't likely to win games against playoff-caliber opponents if their QB can't threaten vertically and take better care of the football.

Secondly, Cousins is acting as a placeholder for No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza .

The Raiders won't want to turn the page to Mendoza before the Indiana product is fully ready. Cousins has to prove that he's still an above-average starter in order to keep the rookie on the bench.

Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has certainly performed like a franchise quarterback in the past. The two-time Pro Bowler even earned an MVP vote last season and earned some lofty praise from his head coach before the start of this season.

Jim Harbaugh told The White House with Michael Irvin (h/t Michael Davis Smith of ProFootballTalk) that he believes that Herbert will one day be known as an all-time great.

However, Herbert was also one of the biggest flops of Week 1. His numbers weren't atrocious (17-of-27 for 209 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT), but he played inefficiently down the stretch, threw a costly fourth-quarter interception, and lost by double digits to the week's biggest underdog.

Herbert has to be better moving forward for a variety of reasons—to give Los Angeles a legitimate shot at a title, to show a partnership with Mike McDaniel can work, and to prove that he belongs in the same conversation with quarterbacks like Josh Allen, Joe Burrow, Lamar Jackson, and Patrick Mahomes.

We're still not 100 percent certain that Aaron Donald will make his 2026 debut on Monday night, but the Los Angeles Rams are hoping to see him on the field.

"Hopefully he's feeling good enough and if he says he's ready to go, then we'll be excited to see him," head coach Sean McVay said, per ESPN's Sarah Barshop .

Under normal circumstances, a 35-year-old defensive tackle wouldn't face lofty expectations coming out of a two-year retirement. However, Donald's situation is not normal. He's arguably the best defender of the NFL's modern era, and he was widely viewed as the final piece of Los Angeles' Super Bowl puzzle.

Just as importantly, the Rams need Donald to step in and make an impact. Their defense looked terrible against the rival San Francisco 49ers in Week 1, and prized trade acquisition and pass-rusher Myles Garrett just went to injured reserve with a knee injury.

Fair or not, the Rams need Donald to prove that he's still the same Pro Bowl-caliber player he was before he walked away for the first time.

The Dolphins aren't expected to win many games in 2026, but they do have a chance to evaluate promising players who could be a big part of the future. The most important player to evaluate is quarterback Malik Willis, who signed a three-year, $67.5 million deal in free agency.

If Willis can show that he's an above-average starter, Miami will have options in a 2027 draft class that is expected to be deep at quarterback.

Of course, properly evaluating any quarterback requires a functional supporting cast. For the Dolphins, that means identifying a No. 1 receiver. They might just have one in rookie third-round pick Caleb Douglas .

Douglas was impressive in Week 1, catching five of seven targets for 94 yards, though he operated against a suspect Raiders defense. He'll need to prove that he can replicate his Week 1 success against the Chargers on Sunday if he hopes to establish himself as Miami's go-to pass-catcher.

The Minnesota Vikings surprised a lot of folks when they used the 18th overall pick on Florida defensive tackle Caleb Banks . While Banks flashed real NFL potential in college, he was also limited to just three games in 2025 by a foot injury.

Banks suffered another foot fracture in February at the scouting combine.

A concerning injury history doesn't guarantee that Banks won't be a terrific contributor for Minnesota. However, he'll have to prove that he can stay healthy and fill a prominent role in the defensive front.

Banks did suit up for Minnesota's opener, but he played just 24 percent of the defensive snaps and finished without a tackle.

Quarterback Drake Maye deserves a dishonorable mention here after struggling in the 2025 playoffs and throwing three interceptions in the 2026 season opener. However, New England Patriots wide receiver Romeo Doubs has even more to prove entering Week 2.

Doubs was a marquee free-agent pickup for the Patriots and signed a four-year, $68 million contract . He was supposed to be a dependable, chain-moving target for Maye but was anything but in his 2026 debut. Doubs failed to catch any of his three targets, was targeted on one of Maye's interceptions, and had a key fourth-quarter drop.

The Patriots desperately need Doubs to prove that he's more reliable than he showed in Week 1 because they recently placed No. 1 receiver A.J. Brown on injured reserve with an ankle injury.

The New Orleans Saints used the 14th pick in the 2024 draft on offensive tackle Taliese Fuaga with the hope that he would help solidify the offensive line. While the Oregon State product has started all 31 games in which he has appeared, he hasn't been a high-end player.

Last season, Fuaga was decidedly average, though he battled knee, ankle, and back injuries and was ultimately limited to 13 games. He wasn't much better against the Lions in Week 1. He allowed a sack and was graded 63rd in pass blocking among tackles by Pro Football Focus .

New Orleans is likely to go as far as second-year quarterback Tyler Shough can take the team this season. The Saints need Fuaga to be better at protecting their quarterback. Fuaga needs to prove that he can be consistently better, too, because he'll be extension-eligible in the offseason.

Back in 2023, the New York Giants used a first-round pick on Maryland cornerback Deonte Banks. While he was a regular starter as a rookie, he was benched toward the end of his second season and only made six starts in 2025.

Though the Giants declined the fifth-year option on Banks' contract, the arrival of new head coach John Harbaugh gave the corner a fresh opportunity to prove himself. While he got the start against the Cowboys in Week 1, Banks wasn't great.

The 25-year-old did log a pair of batted passes, but he also allowed four receptions and surrendered a touchdown. Overall, he allowed an opposing passer rating of 103.0 in coverage.

The Giants need to see more from Banks if they're going to keep him in a starting role, and he has to be better if he has any hope of cashing in during 2027 free agency.

The New York Jets had their pick of prospects not named Fernando Mendoza with the second pick in April's draft, and they opted for Texas Tech edge-rusher David Bailey . This means that, for the foreseeable future, Bailey will be compared to other top rookies in the 2026 class.

Through one full week, Bailey has made the Jets look like geniuses for their selection. He recorded four tackles, a tackle for loss, a sack, and two quarterback pressures in his NFL debut.

Of course, it's worth noting that Bailey's performance came against an inexperienced quarterback and a bad Tennessee Titans offensive line. If he's going to prove that he was the best non-quarterback available in his draft class, Bailey will have to maintain his high level of play against more formidable opponents. He'll get a prime opportunity against the Packers on Sunday.

The Philadelphia Eagles got the win in Week 1, but they learned during the game that Landon Dickerson's knee ailment was something that he shouldn't be playing through. Earlier this week, they placed the standout guard on short-term injured reserve.

While Philly hasn't publicly announced who will replace Dickerson in the starting lineup, 2025 fifth-round pick Drew Kendall is the likeliest candidate. He appeared in seven games with one start as a rookie and is preparing himself to start in Week 2.

"Just feel ready and staying ready for when my name is called. I'm not sure what's going to happen," Kendall said, per Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia.

This will be a massive opportunity for Kendall, who can cement his status as a key reserve if he plays well. It'll also be a big challenge, and the Eagles need Kendall to prove that he's up to the challenge.

While the Titans aren't exactly a daunting Week 2 opponent, Philly has the Bears, Rams, and Jaguars up next on the schedule.

DK Metcalf had an underwhelming Week 1, catching just four of 10 targets for 40 yards. However, Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers doesn't appear to be concerned.

"I'm not worried about DK at all, man," Rodgers said, per Mike DeFabo of The Athletic.

Still, Metcalf needs to prove that his poor performance last Sunday was a fluke for a couple of reasons. For one, the Steelers need a dependable perimeter target opposite Michael Pittman Jr. if they're going to field a playoff-caliber offense this season.

Secondly, Pittman is threatening to take over as Pittsburgh's No. 1 receiver, which would leave Metcalf's future in Pittsburgh uncertain. He's under contract through 2029, but the Steelers could save $26.5 million in 2027 cap space by releasing Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in the spring.

San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle is 32 years old and is coming off a torn Achilles that he suffered in January. Therefore, the fact that he was even on the field for San Francisco's opener was impressive.

However, Kittle didn't have a massive impact on the 49ers' 27-20 win. He obviously commanded some defensive attention, but he caught just two of five targets for 12 yards.

Kittle needs to prove that he can get back to pre-injury form quickly because injuries are already becoming an issue for the 49ers' receiving corps. Ricky Pearsall is out for the year with a PCL injury, and San Francisco recently placed tight end Jake Tonges and promising rookie receiver De'Zhaun Stribling on injured reserve.

According to head coach Kyle Shanahan (h/t Matt Barrows of The Athletic), Stribling (ankle) is expected to miss around 10 weeks, but Tonges (MCL) is done for the season.

The Seattle Seahawks won Super Bowl LX with quarterback Sam Darnold and planned to compete with the 2018 first-rounder again in 2026. However, Darnold was knocked out of Week 1 with what is now being described as a glue injury.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , Darnold is expected to miss roughly four weeks with the injury.

For the foreseeable future, Seattle will have to rely on backup quarterback Drew Lock. He played well enough to defeat the Patriots in Week 1, and he'll have to continue playing well if the Seahawks are going to successfully navigate a long stretch without their starter. His teammates believe he will.

"We all have faith in Drew," defensive lineman Leonard Williams said, per Ari Horton of the team's official website.

If the Seahawks are going to stay near the top of the loaded NFC West, Lock will have to prove that Seattle's faith in him isn't unfounded.

Quarterback Baker Mayfield deserves consideration here. He signed a three-year, $165 million extension just before the start of the season and then proceeded to fumble three times in Week 1.

However, Mayfield largely played well aside from the giveaways. Rookie first-round pick Pueben Bain Jr. was largely invisible. The 15th pick in April's draft played 64 percent of the defensive snaps but finished with just one tackle, no sacks, and no QB pressures.

Bain was arguably college football's most disruptive defender in 2025 but fell in the draft due to concerns about arm length. He needs to prove that such concerns were unwarranted, and he needs to play much, much better to prove the Bucs right for stopping his slide in the middle of Round 1.

As a rookie last season, Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward didn't play up to his draft status as the No. 1 pick in the draft. Of course, the Miami product was saddled with one of the worst supporting casts in the league.

The Titans worked to upgrade their offense in the offseason, adding the likes of center Austin Schlottmann, receiver Wan'Dale Robinson, and rookie wideout Carnell Tate . Unfortunately, Ward (80.2 QB rating) looked a lot like he did as a rookie in Week 1.

Naturally, Tennessee isn't going to simply give up on its young quarterback.

"We're fully committed to Cam because we believe in him," Saleh told ESPN's Turron Davenport . "You've got to let these young men grow."

However, Ward has to start showing tangible growth. Otherwise, the Titans may have to consider sitting him, as the Panthers did with Bryce Young during his sophomore campaign.

Washington Commanders: WR Terry McLaurin

This may seem like an odd choice, as Terry McLaurin has essentially been the Commanders' No. 1 receiver for the past eight seasons. However, he's also 31 years old and is coming off a game in which he was pretty much invisible.

Against the Eagles in Week 1, McLaurin caught just two of four targets for 14 yards. He had less of an impact than recent addition Stefon Diggs, rookie Antonio Williams , and even tight end Chigoziem Okonkwo.

McLaurin needs to prove that he can still be an elite difference maker because A.) Washington needs to support quarterback Jayden Daniels and B.) another disappointing campaign could leave McLaurin as a 2027 cap casualty.

Last season, injuries limited McLaurin to 10 games and 582 receiving yards. Next spring, the Commanders could save $25.5 million in cap space by releasing him with a post-June 1 designation.

articles.title: Cam Skattebo Teases New TD Celebration Despite Viral Video of Backflip in Giants' Win vs. Cowboys
articles.summary: New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo says he's planning on mixing up his end zone celebrations after capping off his first touchdown of the season with a backflip.
articles.body:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo says he's planning on mixing up his end zone celebrations after capping off his first touchdown of the season with a backflip .

"I've been saying it for about a month now, I'm gonna do a backflip when I score my first touchdown," Skattebo said after the Giants kicked off the season last Sunday with a 28-20 win over the visiting Dallas Cowboys.

"I might do it here and there throughout the year, but you won't see it every time. Make up something else now, and try to give the kids something else to do."

18M Views and 'Sheer Ass Whupping,' Tyler Owens' Viral Play Draws More Reaction to Epic Video

Skattebo flipped in the end zone after running in the Cowboys' first touchdown of the game in Sunday's first quarter.

Skattebo finished the win with 18 carries for 81 rushing yards in his first game back after recovering from the right ankle dislocation, tibia fracture and ruptured deltoid ligament that ended his rookie season last October.

The running back, who told Kay Adams earlier this month he contemplated retirement early in his rehab, is set to once more serve as the Giants' lead back when the team kicks off its first road game of the season Monday at the Los Angeles Rams.

articles.title: Is it too early to panic in the NFL? These teams don’t want to find out
articles.summary: Sixteen NFL teams, including some with big playoff aspirations like the Dallas Cowboys and Los Angeles Rams, are trying to avoid falling to 0-2.
articles.body: When the Cleveland Browns, the Tennessee Titans and the Atlanta Falcons opened the new NFL season 0-1 last week, it wasn’t a surprise. Each is considered far likelier to contend for the league’s worst record than a playoff berth. Yet entering the season’s second week, it might be time for some other members of the 0-1 club to be feeling panic. The so-far winless Los Angeles Rams and Chargers, New England Patriots, Dallas Cowboys, Green Bay Packers, Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Denver Broncos all entered the season with justified playoff ambitions — plans that would be further jeopardized by starting 0-2. Since the AFL-NFL merger in 1970, only 11% of 0-2 teams have gone on to make the postseason. The expansion of the playoff format to 14 teams in 2020 has made rebounding slightly easier; since then, 16% of 0-2 teams have gone on to make the postseason, including three each of the last two seasons. But a stumble to open September whittles away a team’s margin for error. Baltimore missed last season’s playoffs when its field goal missed in the season finale, circumstances that might have been avoided had the Ravens not started 1-5. Kansas City stumbled to an 0-2 start last season and spent the next two months digging itself out of that hole before it missed the playoffs for the first time in a decade. “My message is just echoing ‘don’t change, don’t flinch, don’t blink,’” Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott said. “This is a long year. We have to stick together.” Two seasons ago, the Rams were one of three teams that started 0-2 and still made the playoffs. But as the Rams, the preseason Super Bowl favorite, prepare to face the Giants (1-0) on Monday, they have already lost more than their first game. Pass-rushing star Myles Garrett will miss at least four games after he underwent surgery last week to combat swelling in his left knee. The un-retirement of Aaron Donald will help absorb the loss of Garrett along the defensive line, but Donald won’t be an every-down player. The Rams’ vaunted offense managed just 190 yards in its first performance against the San Francisco 49ers, as well. “The big area of focus improvement will be in regard to the pass game and some of the different things that we can do collectively,” coach Sean McVay said. “It always starts with me.” The Rams are one of five teams this season — joining the Broncos, the Packers, the Cowboys and the Washington Commanders — that already have one division loss. Of that group, NFC East rivals Washington and Dallas find themselves in the most precarious situations. When they play each other Sunday, one will leave 0-2 in its division. “It’s another division game,” Cowboys pass rusher Rashan Gary said. “Understanding that, we know we just went 0-1, and we can’t do that going into this week. The urgency is up, for sure.” The Patriots have been here before. Last season they responded to their 0-1 start by losing only two more times over the next four months en route to a Super Bowl appearance. The bounceback was helped, however, by playing the easiest schedule in 26 years. It will be more difficult to keep this latest season-opening loss from snowballing into something bigger. The Patriots’ next three opponents all made the playoffs last season, starting with Sunday’s matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers — whose defense sacked New England quarterback Drake Maye five times and forced five turnovers when the teams met last season. An injured ankle will sideline the Steelers’ top offseason acquisition, receiver A.J. Brown, for at least the next four games. “We’ve said this for as long as I can remember: The teams that continue to improve are going to be the ones that have a chance at the end,” Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said. Though there is at least one 0-1 team in all eight NFL divisions, some fared worse than others. Three of the four AFC South teams lost, with the Jacksonville Jaguars the lone outlier. The entire NFC South, meanwhile, is 0-1, including the Carolina Panthers, who have started 0-2 each of the last four seasons. When division rivals Atlanta and Carolina play Sunday, one is guaranteed to leave 0-2. It is one of three Week 2 games featuring winless teams, ensuring that one team will stay that way, joining Cowboys-Commanders and Cleveland-Tampa Bay. Sometimes, an 0-1 start feels worse than one game would indicate. Green Bay’s 17-point loss to division rival Minnesota was the Packers’ sixth consecutive defeat dating to last season, the franchise’s longest losing streak since 1990-91. It was also their third consecutive divisional loss after having held a double-digit lead. Green Bay had led Chicago by 10 in December and again by 18 in a January playoff game, only to lose. When Green Bay lost its 12-point lead en route to a blowout Sunday, the collapse revived alarm bells about the team’s ability to close out games. “It’s going to be a topic of conversation for you guys until we do it,” coach Matt LaFleur told reporters Sunday. “That’s the bottom line.” Said quarterback Jordan Love: “All these games find ways to be close at the end. We’ve got to find ways to be at our best. We’ve talked about it time and time again, and I think we’ll keep talking about it until we figure it out and do something about it.” Perhaps the team that is most unexpectedly trying to avoid an 0-2 hole is the Chargers, who were given the eighth-best odds to win the Super Bowl, only to be outplayed thoroughly at home by Arizona, a team that was expected to be near the bottom of the standings. The loss aggravated criticism of quarterback Justin Herbert and the Chargers’ lack of protection for him. Since 2020, when Herbert entered the league, no other quarterback has been sacked more times (228). That total includes the three he took against the Cardinals, including one much-publicized play in which three Chargers blockers teamed up on one Cardinals defender, allowing two to rush free at Herbert. “It feels like it does in any fight — feels like it does in a football fight where you don’t win,” coach Jim Harbaugh said. “Your mind says, ‘What are you going to do about it?’” It’s the question facing all 16 of the NFL’s winless teams entering Week 2.

articles.title: 18M Views and 'Sheer Ass Whupping,' Tyler Owens' Viral Play Draws More Reaction to Epic Video
articles.summary: JJ Watt was apparently not the only person around the NFL world impressed by last Sunday's highlight-reel special teams run from Washington Commanders safety Tyler Owens.
articles.body:
JJ Watt was apparently not the only person around the NFL world impressed by last Sunday's highlight-reel special teams run from Washington Commanders safety Tyler Owens.

The clip, which Watt praised as "legitimately one of the greatest football plays I've ever seen," showed Owens shoving his way between two Eagles blockers on punt coverage before fighting his way downfield to complete a tackle.

The post received 18 million views on a single social media platform, per ESPN's John Keim .

Cam Skattebo Teases New TD Celebration Despite Viral Video of Backflip in Giants' Win vs. Cowboys

The video also drew praise from Commanders special teams coach Larry Izzo, who described the play to Keim as "just a sheer ass whupping."

"When you combine that mindset and that play style with the freakish skill-set he has, that's what you're left with, which is an exceptional play, one that in 30 years in the NFL I don't know if I've seen a better demonstration of just a dude whupping people's asses," Izzo told Keim.

Owens is playing in his third season with the Commanders after taking the field for 84 percent of Washington's special teams snaps last season.

His dominant play last weekend might draw him some extra attention from Dallas Cowboys coaches game-planning for punt returns during Saturday's Week 2 matchup in Arlington. Kickoff between the Cowboys and visiting Commanders is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Drake Maye spent his childhood studying Aaron Rodgers on YouTube now he's replacing him as the NFL's next star
articles.summary: NFL News: When Drake Maye was nine years old, he watched Aaron Rodgers dismantle the Pittsburgh Steelers in Super Bowl XLV. That game didn't just stick with him.
articles.body: When Drake Maye was nine years old, he watched Aaron Rodgers dismantle the Pittsburgh Steelers in Super Bowl XLV. That game didn't just stick with him. It shaped him. Maye started studying Rodgers obsessively, right down to his throwing motion and pregame warmup routine. Fast forward to 2025, and the same kid is now an NFL starter, getting compared to Rodgers by opposing coaches, while Rodgers himself is winding down what could be his final season at 41.How did Drake Maye become so obsessed with Aaron Rodgers growing up?It wasn't just casual admiration. Maye carried an Aaron Rodgers phone case for years. He would pull up warmup clips on YouTube trying to decode how Rodgers gripped the ball and released it. "Shoot, it's hard to emulate the way he spins it. I mean, he spins it with the best of 'em," Maye said recently. That kind of fixation from a young quarterback is unusual. Most kids pick a favorite player. Maye picked a blueprint.The Patriots selected Maye with the third overall pick in the 2024 draft, and from the moment he arrived in New England, the Rodgers comparisons followed him. He even got his boyhood moment when the Patriots faced the Jets in Week 3 of 2024. After the game, Maye lingered on the field, waiting. "I'm waiting for the GOAT," he told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo. He finally approached Rodgers, shook his hand, and said, "Big fan. Best of luck." Rodgers kept whatever he said next to himself. A private conversation, he noted.That moment felt symbolic. The veteran acknowledging the kid quietly. The kid still starstruck but clearly ready.Is Drake Maye already playing like Aaron Rodgers in the NFL?The numbers in his second season suggest something real is developing. Maye has thrown for 1,744 yards with 12 touchdowns and just two interceptions, ranking sixth in the league in passing yards. An anonymous NFL coach watching him carved up the Titans told The Athletic's Mike Sando that a deep ball Maye threw to Mack Hollins on a 93-yard scoring drive was flat-out "Rodgers-like." That's not a throwaway comparison. That's a defensive coach, watching tape, reaching for one specific name.Rodgers, meanwhile, just beat the Patriots in Week 3 of the 2025 season, 21-14, throwing the game-winning touchdown with two minutes left. He had the last word that day. But Maye, who finished with a 102.1 passer rating in that loss, isn't far behind. The gap is closing faster than anyone expected.What makes this storyline different from the usual passing-of-the-torch narrative is that Maye didn't just idolize Rodgers from a distance. He studied him the way a student studies a subject. Every warmup rep. Every release point. Now those lessons are showing up on actual NFL Sundays, against actual NFL defenses.Rodgers threw his first NFL touchdown pass in 2005. articles.title: No. 4 Buford football stays perfect after ‘The Grizzy’ gives them special teams magic
articles.summary: Buford remained undefeated after a surprise fake field goal touchdown by Ian Chafin helped beat Grayson 23-13.
articles.body:
Two Georgia powerhouses. Two of the state's most recent state championship teams. Yet, somehow, two teams that had never met in a regular-season game.

From the moment No. 4 Buford and Grayson stepped onto the field Friday night, Sept. 18, it was clear that this game was going to be anything but a normal high school football game.

And that ended up being true in Buford's 23-13 win over Grayson at Britt-Moody Field.

With a 16-13 lead in the fourth quarter, Buford drove into the red zone but failed to turn the possession into a touchdown. With seven minutes remaining, The Wolves' special teams unit took the field, looking to turn a three-point lead into six.

Senior holder Ian Chafin took the snap, hopped up, spotted a hole to his right and ran straight into the end zone without a single Grayson defender touching him.

"I didn't think it was going to be that open," Chafin said after the game. "My teammates made it happen. They opened the hole for me and I just ran in and took advantage of the opportunity."

For Chafin, the play had been perfected long before he took the field Friday night. The Wolves had been practicing "The Grizzly" all week, and thanks to a call from special teams coordinator Drew Dasher, they finally got the chance to unleash it.

"I told (Dasher) earlier in the week, 'If you've got the chance to do something, do it,'" head coach Bryant Appling said. "And he wasn't scared to do it. It was the perfect call in the perfect situation."

Dasher took the chance — and picked the right guy to execute it.

"I had to get in," Chafin said. "There was no doubt I had to get in. I had to change the game right there."

See photos of the best high school football celebrations from Week 5

Although the Rams still had plenty of time to make something happen, the touchdown shifted the momentum squarely towards the Wolves, who suddenly had a 10-point lead with seven minutes remaining.

That touchdown marked Chafin's first of the season and the second of his career, according to MaxPreps.

"He's come a long way," Appling said. "He's a great leader, he's a hard worker, he's doing everything the way we need him to do it. For him to have the chance like that in a big game to make a special play like that, it's huge."

The Wolves got off to a slow start on both sides of the ball, with their first two offensive drives ending in an interception and a three-and-out. Their first two defensive drives, meanwhile, resulted in a Grayson field goal and a touchdown.

But after falling into a 10-0 deficit, Buford settled in.

"Our kids were too up and trying to make plays and that's how things go," Appling said. "But we found a way to play our brand of football against a really good defense and a really good team down the stretch."

For the next three quarters, the Wolves defense held the Rams to just one field goal.

Senior Brady Wagner led that defense with six tackles, including 2.5 for loss, and 1.5 sacks.

It's hard to mention Buford's defense without also mentioning its newest addition: five-star defensive lineman Jalen Brewster. Although he made his debut last weekend against Miami Central, the Texas Tech commit got his first taste of Georgia high school football against the Rams.

"It's definitely from the trenches — Georgia," Brewster said. "I'm getting used to Buford and Georgia and just really getting used to the scheme and the way they play ball down here."

Buford walks away from its difficult opening four-game slate still undefeated.

"It's everything for us," Chafin said. "We need this momentum going into region play and then into playoffs."

articles.title: 2027 NFL Draft: QBs to watch in Week 3 of college football
articles.summary: Here are three quarterbacks Cleveland Browns fans must watch during Week 3 of the 2026 college football season.
articles.body:
While Cleveland Browns fans continue to muddle their way through the 2026-27 NFL season, the struggling fanbase has the 2027 NFL Draft to look forward to throughout the course of the regular season.

Last week, the quarterback tracker highlighted Texas' Arch Manning , who led his squad to an impressive 20+ point comeback against the Ohio State Buckeyes . Now, as we enter Week Three of the 2026 college football season, there is a new batch of quarterbacks Browns fans must keep their eyes on.

Here are three quarterbacks Browns fans must watch during Week Three of the college football season.

Saturday, 4:15 PM EST vs. Mississippi State (SEC Network)

South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers finally makes his first appearance on the college quarterback tracker this season.

At 6-foot-3, 245 lbs., Sellers possesses all the tools to become a star at the NFL level. In his two regular-season starts this year, the prolific prospect threw for 366 yards and three touchdowns, while also rushing for 120 yards and a touchdown. Now, Sellers will receive a golden opportunity to boost his stock this weekend in his first conference matchup of the season.

If Sellers can maintain his strong start and outduel rising star Kamario Taylor at home, you may start hearing his name more in first-round conversations.

After a dazzling 2026 debut against the Louisville Cardinals, Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss has caught the attention of many NFL fanbases searching for a quarterback.

Chambliss may not have the ideal frame for a starting quarterback in the NFL (5-foot-11, 208 lbs.), but his clutchness in crunch time has been on point since last year's College Football Playoffs. The electric playmaker is up to 531 passing yards and five touchdowns in his first two games this season against the Cardinals and the Charlotte 49ers.

Unfortunately for Chambliss and the Rebels, the program must take on the red-hot LSU Tigers at home on Saturday evening. This should be another key game for Chambliss as he reviews his film for the upcoming draft .

Saturday, 7:30 PM EST vs. Michigan State (NBC)

It's hard to judge Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr's draft stock after the first two weeks of the college football season due to the lack of competition.

However, despite the easy schedule, Carr continues to show promise during his second season as the Fighting Irish's starting quarterback. When facing both the Wisconsin Badgers and the Rice Owls, Carr threw for 492 passing yards and six touchdowns while completing 71.4 percent of his attempts.

Do the Michigan State Spartans pose a threat to Notre Dame this weekend? Probably not. But if Carr wants to keep his name in the conversation for the 2027 NFL Draft class, he must continue to stack his clean performances against the Big 10 Conference member on Saturday.

articles.title: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan 'Felt Like Crap' for Days After Australia Trip Home
articles.summary: Allowing the San Francisco 49ers to adjust to the time zone change before his team's Week 1 win in Australia apparently took a toll ahead of head coach Kyle Shanahan's preparation for Week 2.
articles.body:
Allowing the San Francisco 49ers to adjust to the time zone change before his team's Week 1 win in Australia apparently took a toll ahead of head coach Kyle Shanahan's preparation for Week 2.

Shanahan told reporters he felt the team was "totally good" as of Wednesday but needed a few days of recovery after returning from last Thursday's 27-7 victory over the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne.

"Speaking for myself, I felt like crap all weekend," Shanahan said. "We had two days off, and I did not feel right. Took a few days. I think I was good by Monday.

"Talking to some of the guys, some guys felt fine right away, some went through the same stuff, but I think we're definitely all good by now."

There is a 17-hour time difference between San Francisco and Melbourne, in which the 49ers arrived a week before the season opener.

Niners fullback Kyle Juszczyk recently told The MMQB's Albert Breer it took him "about three days" to adjust after arriving.

The Rams took a different approach to the time zone change, arriving in Melbourne at dawn the day before the game as part of head coach Sean McVay's efforts to keep his team on California time.

That theoretically could make jet-lag recovery ahead of Week 2 easier, but it didn't pay off in Australia. After taking an early lead on a second-quarter touchdown, the Rams did not score again in the blowout loss.

Both teams' struggles with the time changes raises a potential obstacle to what NFL commissioner Roger Goodell has repeatedly said is the league's hope of someday expanding outside the United States.

For now, Shanahan and the 49ers will focus on playing their first home-country game of the season Sunday against the visiting Miami Dolphins. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET in Santa Clara.

articles.title: In 2026, a collector paid $25,000 to start bidding on Tom Brady’s Patriots jersey; it was tied to his 2019 Peyton Manning milestone and sold for $273,107
articles.summary: NFL News: Tom Brady’s game-worn New England Patriots jersey from a memorable 2019 game against the New York Giants has now sold for $273,107 at auction. Brady w.
articles.body: Tom Brady’s game-worn New England Patriots jersey from a memorable 2019 game against the New York Giants has now sold for $273,107 at auction. Brady wore the jersey on a night when he passed Peyton Manning to move into second place on the NFL’s all-time passing yards list. The jersey was sold through Grey Flannel Auctions after attracting 24 bids.Tom Brady jersey from historic Patriots win draws major interestThe jersey came from New England’s 35-14 win over the Giants on October 10, 2019. Brady had a strong night, completing 31 passes for 334 yards while also scoring two rushing touchdowns. The game became even more important because his passing total pushed him past Manning on the NFL’s career list.Grey Flannel Auctions listed the jersey with an opening bid of $25,000. During the auction, interest continued to grow, with the highest reported bid reaching $203,507 before the auction closed. The auction house later listed the final sale at $273,107, with 24 bids recorded.The jersey was part of Grey Flannel’s August 16, 2026 Photo-Matched Auction. The auction ran from July 24 through August 16, with the prices shown by the auction house including the buyer’s premium.Why the 2019 game made Brady’s jersey specialBrady’s performance against the Giants was not just another regular-season game. Passing Manning on the career passing yards list gave the jersey a direct connection to an important point in Brady’s career.The item also came with authentication and photo-matching documentation. According to the auction listing, the jersey had an NFL certificate of authenticity and a MeiGray photo match. The MeiGray documentation noted identifying details on the jersey, helping connect the actual piece of clothing to Brady’s use during the game.That kind of documentation matters in the sports memorabilia market. A jersey can become much more valuable when collectors can connect it to one specific game or achievement rather than simply showing that it belonged to a famous player.Brady’s memorabilia has already reached much higher prices. His final NFL game-worn Tampa Bay Buccaneers jersey sold for $1.391 million through RM Sotheby’s in 2023. The jersey was worn during his final game against the Dallas Cowboys and was photo-matched to the third and fourth quarters.In 2026, Joe Montana’s Super Bowl XXIV jersey also set a new reported NFL jersey record at $1.515 million, according to Goldin. That sale moved past Brady’s 2023 result.Still, the $273,107 price for Brady’s 2019 Patriots jersey shows how much collectors value items tied to specific moments from his career. This was not simply a jersey worn during a Patriots win. It was the jersey Brady wore when he moved past Manning on the NFL’s passing yards list, giving the piece a clear place in football history.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body:
Whatever feelings Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield might about how his tenure with the Cleveland Browns ended reportedly isn't visibly impacting his preparation for Week 2.

The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported Saturday "multiple Tampa Bay Buccaneers sources tell me they have seen no change in [Mayfield's] demeanor this week before facing his old team."

Mayfield signed a three-year, $165 million extension with the Buccaneers shortly before struggling last weekend in his team's season-opening loss to the Cincinnati Bengals.

The quarterback committed three turnovers as the Bucs conceded a 33-27 loss to the Bengals last Sunday.

Mayfield was selected at the top of the 2018 draft by the Browns and played four seasons for the franchise before he was traded in 2022 to the Carolina Panthers for a conditional fifth-round pick.

The Browns acquired and extended Deshaun Watson the same year, only to see Watson's career derailed by suspensions and injuries.

"When there's history between a franchise, a coaching staff, anybody, there's always— you want to come out on the winning side, no matter what," Mayfield said earlier this week about facing his former team. "Obviously, it's very different there, staff-wise, and everybody."

When asked how he planned to not let emotions impact him, Mayfield answered, "Really focusing on the small details. When you do that, good things will happen on Sunday."

Watson, who saw his first NFL action since 2024 in the Browns' season-opening loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, will matchup against Mayfield for the first time since both quarterbacks were traded in 2022 this Sunday at 1 p.m. ET in Tampa.

articles.title: 'Very Messy,' Rival NFL Exec Explains Sean Payton-Davis Webb Concern After Broncos' Struggles
articles.summary: After a lackluster Week 1 performance, Davis Webb's status as offensive play-caller for the Denver Broncos already appears to be on some thin ice.
articles.body:
After a lackluster Week 1 performance, Davis Webb's status as offensive play-caller for the Denver Broncos already appears to be on some thin ice.

Per The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , one executive from a rival AFC club explained things could get "very messy" between Webb and head coach Sean Payton if the Broncos have a slow start on Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars:

"I think Sean's play calling last year was unbelievable. He is such an elite play caller. Davis is a good dude, but he's 31 and never called plays before. That's going to be an interesting situation. They have a helluva schedule. They have a tough one against Jacksonville. If they come out of the gates slowly, it's gonna be hard for Sean to stick with this. That would get very messy."

2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 2 🏈

One of the most surprising moves of the NFL offseason was Payton announcing in February that he was ceding play-calling duties for the offense to Webb.

The decision came as Webb was generating a lot of interest as a head coaching candidate. He was reportedly viewed as a "strong" option for the Las Vegas Raiders, and he interviewed with the Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens.

Webb wound up withdrawing his name from consideration for the Raiders job. The 31-year-old has only been coaching since the 2023 season when he was hired by Payton to join Denver's staff. He was the quarterbacks coach for three seasons, and added the title of offensive pass game coordinator in 2025.

Webb had no prior play-calling experience before being named Broncos offensive coordinator in February. It also marked the first time in Payton's head-coaching career dating back to his first season with the New Orleans Saints in 2006 that he wasn't calling plays for the offense.

The entirety of Denver's performance in a 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 1 was a disappointment, but the offense putting up 176 yards and nine first downs led to a lot of scrutiny around the play-calling.

Even though Payton came to Webb's defense , it's hard to envision a head coach who is as hands-on as Payton has been throughout his career not taking control if he thinks things are spiraling in the wrong direction.

Sunday's game against a Jaguars defense that gave Denver plenty of problems in their Week 16 matchup last season could go a long way toward determining if Webb holds onto his job or if Payton steps back in.

Tank Dell, who is still working his way back from a serious knee injury suffered in Week 16 of the 2024 season, was placed on the PUP list to start this year and will miss at least the first four games.

Collins led the Texans in targets (10), receptions (seven), receiving yards (75) and caught a touchdown pass in a 36-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 1.

That distinction is worth understanding. Under the NFL's disciplinary review process , the league reviews every play and can issue fines for violations that were not penalized during the game.

Players also have the right to appeal. The supplied report does not indicate whether Gibbs plans to challenge this one.

Gibbs was a major part of Detroit's opening-week offense, handling 29 carries in the Lions' 31–30 overtime victory. His workload and ability were among the concerns highlighted in Buffalo's preparation for Detroit's offense .
